name: Ransomware Payment Laundering
description: Ransomware operators demand payment in virtual assets and then launder proceeds through chains of wallets, mixers, exchanges and over-the-counter brokers. Victims and their facilitators, such as incident response firms and insurers, also create exposure. Institutions may detect either victim payments or operator cash-out.

sources.text: FinCEN, Advisory on Ransomware and the Use of the Financial System to Facilitate Ransom Payments (FIN-2021-A004, 2021)
FATF, Virtual Assets: Red Flag Indicators of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (2020)

exposure.rationale: Victim payments via exchanges/OTC and operator cash-out; insurers and IR facilitators.

indicators.name: Customer purchases virtual assets and sends them immediately to a new wallet
indicators.canon: Customer purchases virtual assets and sends them immediately to a new wallet
indicators.desc: A first-time or unsophisticated buyer buys a large amount and withdraws it all to an unfamiliar address, consistent with a victim ransom payment.
indicators.ctx: A first-time or unsophisticated buyer buys a large amount and withdraws it all to an unfamiliar address, consistent with a victim ransom payment.

indicators.name: Corporate account pays an unusual crypto purchase after a cyber event
indicators.canon: Corporate account pays an unusual crypto purchase after a cyber event
indicators.desc: Business customer suddenly funds a crypto purchase beyond normal activity, with mention of an IT incident or urgent deadline.
indicators.ctx: Business customer suddenly funds a crypto purchase beyond normal activity, with mention of an IT incident or urgent deadline.

indicators.name: Withdrawal address attributed to ransomware actors
indicators.canon: Wallet attributed to ransomware or theft actors
indicators.desc: Source or destination address is attributed to ransomware affiliates, theft or designated actors.
indicators.ctx: Destination or source wallet is attributed to ransomware affiliates or flagged in published designations.

indicators.name: Inbound funds from many victim-like wallets then rapid layering
indicators.canon: Account receiving funds from multiple apparent fraud victims
indicators.desc: A new or low-activity account receives payments from several unrelated individuals who appear to be victims of fraud or phishing, followed by onward movement or cash-out.
indicators.ctx: Account collects payments of similar sizes from unrelated first-time wallets and moves them on within a short period.

indicators.name: Large conversion into privacy coins or mixer use after receipt
indicators.canon: Use of mixers, privacy coins or privacy pools around platform activity
indicators.desc: Funds pass through mixers, privacy coins or privacy-preserving pools before or after platform activity without commercial rationale.
indicators.ctx: Receipts are converted into privacy-enhanced assets or sent to mixing services before exit.

indicators.name: Use of OTC desks or brokers with minimal due diligence
indicators.canon: Use of OTC desks or brokers with minimal due diligence for conversion to fiat
indicators.desc: Large over-the-counter trades or fiat off-ramps via brokers that avoid identity verification, pay via third parties or operate outside strong supervision.
indicators.ctx: Large OTC trades for customers that avoid identity verification or pay via third parties.

indicators.name: Third-party payer funds purchase on behalf of a victim
indicators.canon: Third-party payer funds purchase on behalf of a victim
indicators.desc: Incident response firm, broker or insurer funds crypto on behalf of a client, with unclear client identity or authorisation.
indicators.ctx: Incident response firm, broker or insurer funds crypto on behalf of a client, with unclear client identity or authorisation.
indicators.fp: Legitimate professional ransom-negotiation services, subject to sanctions checks.

indicators.name: Chain-hopping or bridge usage after a large inbound payment
indicators.canon: Chain-hopping through bridges shortly after receipt
indicators.desc: Virtual assets are moved across chains or bridges and converted soon after being received.
indicators.ctx: Funds are moved across chains and wrapped tokens shortly after receipt to break attribution.

indicators.name: Cash-out in jurisdictions with weak controls
indicators.canon: Counterparty or flows in higher-risk jurisdictions with weak AML controls
indicators.desc: Funds, counterparties or institutions are located in jurisdictions with weak AML supervision, sanctions exposure or limited VASP regulation.
indicators.ctx: Final withdrawals go to exchanges or accounts in jurisdictions with poor AML supervision or known to shelter cybercriminals.

indicators.name: Account use inconsistent with prior low-risk behaviour
indicators.canon: Account use inconsistent with prior low-risk behaviour
indicators.desc: Dormant or low-activity account abruptly receives or sends large volumes in a pattern tied to publicised ransomware campaigns.
indicators.ctx: Dormant or low-activity account abruptly receives or sends large volumes in a pattern tied to publicised ransomware campaigns.
